reference_items.figure_description:
A square grid of 7 rows and 7 columns. The left portion (columns 1 through 3) contains a repeating pattern of black house-shaped pentagons (a square base with a triangular roof pointing upward) on a white background:
- Column 2 contains full upward-pointing black house shapes centered horizontally.
- Column 3 contains upward-pointing black house shapes vertically staggered relative to those in column 2.
- Column 1 (along the left edge) and the right half of column 3 contain partial black house shapes where the pattern appears cut off.
Columns 4 through 7 are completely white, except that the cell in row 4, column 5 (counting from the top-left) contains a bold letter 'X'.

reference_items.figure_description:
Three geometric figures composed of small congruent right triangles:
- Figure 1: A single square with a diagonal line from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner, dividing it into two right triangles labeled '1' (top-left) and '2' (bottom-right). Below the square is the label 'Figure 1'.
- Figure 2: A square divided into a 2-by-2 grid of 4 smaller squares. Each smaller square has a diagonal from bottom-left to top-right, creating 8 congruent triangles numbered 1 through 8: top-left square has 1 (upper) and 2 (lower); top-right square has 3 (upper) and 4 (lower); bottom-left square has 5 (upper) and 6 (lower); bottom-right square has 7 (upper) and 8 (lower). Below is the label 'Figure 2'.
- Figure 3: A square divided into a 3-by-3 grid of 9 smaller squares. Each smaller square has a diagonal from bottom-left to top-right, creating 18 congruent triangles. None of the triangles are numbered. Below is the label 'Figure 3'.

reference_items.figure_description:
At the top, four square tiles labeled A, B, C, and D are shown in a row. Each tile is divided conceptually into four smaller quadrants:
- Tile A: A shaded black triangle in the upper-left corner (formed by the diagonal connecting the midpoint of the top edge and the midpoint of the left edge) and a solid black square in the lower-right quadrant.
- Tile B: A shaded black triangle in the upper-right corner and a solid black square in the lower-left quadrant.
- Tile C: A solid black square in the upper-left quadrant and a shaded black triangle in the lower-right corner.
- Tile D: A solid black square in the upper-right quadrant and a shaded black triangle in the lower-left corner.

Below is a 4-by-4 square grid of 16 unit squares, divided into four 2-by-2 quadrants by a vertical line PQ and a horizontal line RS. P is at the top of the vertical line, Q is at the bottom; R is at the left of the horizontal line, S is at the right. Four squares are already labeled:
- Row 1 (top), column 1 (left): 'D'
- Row 2, column 4 (right): 'C'
- Row 3, column 2: 'B'
- Row 4 (bottom), column 3: 'A'
The remaining 12 squares are blank.

reference_items.figure_description:
A 4-by-4 square grid of 16 unit squares, divided into four 2-by-2 quadrants by a vertical line AB (with A at the top, B at the bottom) and a horizontal line CD (with C at the left, D at the right).
Two quadrants are shaded with tile patterns:
- Top-right 2-by-2 quadrant (rows 1-2, columns 3-4):
  - Row 1, column 3: small black square in the top-left corner.
  - Row 1, column 4: small black square in the top-right corner.
  - Row 2, column 3: small black square in the bottom-left corner.
  - Row 2, column 4: small black square in the bottom-right corner.
  - In the center of this 2-by-2 quadrant (where the four squares meet), a large black diamond (rotated square) is formed across the inner corners of all four squares.
- Bottom-left 2-by-2 quadrant (rows 3-4, columns 1-2):
  - Shaded with the exact same pattern: four small black corner squares at the outer corners of the 2-by-2 quadrant, and a large black diamond centered where the four squares meet.
The top-left 2-by-2 quadrant and bottom-right 2-by-2 quadrant are entirely blank (unshaded).

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
